analysis.title: "Somewhat Alarming": Goldman Trader Asks If A Cyber Wave Helped Sink AI Stocks As Critical Vulnerabilities Explode 10x
key_insights: Goldman EMEA head of delta-one trading Rich Privorotsky, in his Friday 'GS Basics' note, called the pace of security incidents 'somewhat alarming'. On Oct 21 a PHP flaw pair, a Java certificate-validation flaw and a malicious LiteLLM release on PyPI and Docker all landed at once. He wondered whether this contributed to the AI concerns the day before.

Wiz disclosed 'PHP2Shell', two memory-safety flaws in PHP's core engine (CVSS up to 9.2) that allow unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP powers about 70% of websites, and per Wiz every PHP version released in the last decade has at least one of the bugs. The researchers found them using AI.

Oracle issued an emergency alert for CVE-2026-91403 (CVSS 9.1), a flaw in how Java applications validate certificate chains. An attacker could forge certificates and make a malicious site appear trusted.

LiteLLM, an open-source AI gateway library with about 23 million weekly downloads, had a malicious release pushed to PyPI and Docker, its second supply chain attack this year. The payload steals cloud credentials, SSH keys and login files for AI coding tools. Per Wiz, attackers were testing stolen AWS credentials against Amazon Bedrock about 4.5 hours later.

An Epoch AI chart of critical and high severity vulnerabilities disclosed by 21 major tech organizations shows monthly counts of roughly 100 to 500 for three years, then a sharp rise. High-severity CVEs now run at roughly 2,900 a month, about 10x the 2022-2025 norm, and critical ones at around 600 (approximate, read off the chart). The inflection is marked at the announcement of Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview.
Epoch cautions that reporting procedures, labeling and cadence vary substantially between organizations, so part of the rise may be more bugs being found rather than more bugs existing.

Wiz says its researchers used frontier models (Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol) for discovery, exploit development and patch validation. One researcher did in a week what would have taken a world-class team months. A Chinese open-weight model already matches Mythos on some cybersecurity tasks, per an earlier ZeroHedge piece from June.

Privorotsky says that in hindsight this 'feels quite bullish for cybersecurity'. AI is cutting the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities while the attack surface grows with token growth. He finds it hard to imagine security spending does not accelerate materially, and asks where the secondary impacts show up across software, cloud infrastructure and the broader digital economy.
This reverses March, when cybersecurity stocks fell on the first reports of Anthropic's 'step change' model, on fears that AI would make defenders obsolete.

Reports this week say major US banks are detecting unauthorized AI agents accessing customer accounts. Schwab and JPMorgan restricted third-party AI agents earlier in the week. Goldman TMT specialist Sean Johnstone notes that David Sacks argues much of this is customers handing credentials to their own AI assistants, a potential breach of bank terms rather than necessarily a cyberattack. Morgan Stanley says it has not seen rogue agents on its platforms. Johnstone adds that customer consent alone does not resolve risks around transaction authority, unintended actions and liability.

Goldman's FX desk (Matt Atherton) listed 'negative AI-related news flow (PHP hacking & US banking issues with AI agents)' alongside capex cuts and borrowing costs in this week's 'semi-perfect storm' of catalysts for the AI selloff.

ZeroHedge's view is that cyber probably did not sink AI stocks on its own. The bigger driver is the price of money: Meta CDS at a record, junk spreads through Goldman's downside case, and a hedge fund de-grossing. Cyber is an added cost for the AI trade, since companies must patch faster, rotate credentials more often and budget for a growing attack surface.
ZeroHedge will watch next week's hyperscaler earnings calls for mentions of security spend and guesses the number will be higher than anyone modeled.

sector_views.rationale: Privorotsky says AI is lowering the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities while the attack surface grows, so security spending should accelerate materially. He calls the incident wave 'quite bullish for cybersecurity'.

Negative AI-related news flow (PHP hacking, US banking issues with AI agents) was listed by Goldman's FX desk among the catalysts for the AI selloff, alongside capex cuts and borrowing costs. Cyber adds a new cost line to the AI trade.

earnings_insights: ZeroHedge expects next week's hyperscaler earnings calls to mention security spend, with a figure higher than anyone modeled. This is the author's guess, not a company or desk estimate.
risk_factors: Simultaneous critical vulnerabilities in PHP (CVSS up to 9.2), Java (CVSS 9.1) and the Python ecosystem (LiteLLM supply chain attack).
AI lowers the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, and the same capability is available to attackers, including open-weight models.
Unauthorized AI agents accessing US bank customer accounts raise open questions on transaction authority, unintended actions and liability.
Higher security spend, faster patching and credential rotation add costs to companies running AI and software stacks.
Epoch data caveat: reporting procedures vary across organizations, so the vulnerability count may partly reflect more detection.
charts_described: Epoch AI chart of critical and high severity vulnerabilities disclosed by 21 major tech organizations (Adobe, Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Oracle and others). Monthly counts bounced between roughly 100 and 500 for three years, then rose sharply. A dotted line marks the announcement of Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview as the start of the rise.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's Privorotsky titled his note 'Systematic Unwinds. Repricing AI Capital Costs. Cyber Incidents'. The article references a hedge fund de-grossing 'for the history books', Meta CDS at a record and junk spreads through Goldman's downside case, all as part of the AI cost-of-capital story.
geopolitical: A Chinese open-weight model already matches Anthropic's Mythos on some cybersecurity tasks, per ZeroHedge's June reference.
cross_bank_references: Morgan Stanley says it has not seen rogue agents on its platforms.
Schwab and JPMorgan restricted third-party AI agents earlier in the week.

tension_points.bull_case: Privorotsky says the incident wave is bullish for cybersecurity: AI cuts the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities while the attack surface grows with token growth, so security spending should accelerate materially.
tension_points.bear_case: For the AI trade and the wider digital economy it is another cost. Companies must patch faster, rotate credentials more often and budget for a growing attack surface, on top of capital that is no longer cheap.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's hyperscaler earnings calls: no mention of higher security spend would undercut the thesis that spending accelerates.

theme_stances.evidence: Hard to imagine security spending doesn't accelerate materially
